title: Korean Plant-Based Mince Noodles
subtitle: with Broccoli and Sesame
description: Explore the wonderful world of Korean cooking. Starring slippery noodles, plant-based mince and a sweet and spicy sauce, it's a vegetarian flavour bomb.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Coarsely chop the broccoli stem into 1cm chunks. Cut the head into small florets. Peel the carrot, then thinly slice on an angle. Thinly slice the spring onion, keeping the white and green parts separate. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves.

Stir-fry mince: Put the chilli paste (see Make it yours), 3 tsp soy sauce, 2 tsp white vinegar, 1 tbs honey and 180ml (¾ cup) water in a bowl and stir to combine. Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium deep frypan over high heat. Stir-fry the plant-based mince for 3-4 mins until browned. Remove from the pan and cover to keep warm.

Stir-fry veggies: Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in the same pan over high heat. Stir-fry the broccoli stem, broccoli florets, carrot, white part of the spring onion, garlic and a pinch of pepper for 2-3 mins until tender but still with crunch. Add the chilli paste mixture, then bring to the boil.

Soak noodles: Reduce the heat to low and cook for 5 mins or until the sauce is slightly thickened. Remove the pan from the heat. Meanwhile, put half the noodles in a large heatproof bowl, cover generously with boiling water and soak for 2 mins, using a fork to gently separate the noodles after they start to soften. Drain.
Serve up: Divide the noodles among bowls. Top with the mince and veggie mixture, then scatter over the sesame seeds and remaining spring onion. Toss to combine and enjoy!

Make it yours: Korean chilli paste, also known as gochujang, is a staple in every Korean pantry. It is slightly sweet, earthy and has a chilli kick. We've suggested this amount for flavour, but feel free to reduce to taste if you prefer less heat.
